items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I've been a great friend of Jean-Marie Masse and his family ever since then.

ctx.x: I was supposed to have played a concert in a town called Limoges with Edouard's band and Don Byas before the band broke up, but missed the gig because I thought that I knew how to get the railroad station we were to leave from with the metro.(subway) I did get to the station which was gare d' Austerlitz, but too late for the train the others had taken because I went the wrong direction inthe subway. No one I came in contact with at the station could speak english. I tried to find out if there was another train…

I stayed with Jean-Marie whose wife's name was Paulette, They had a daughter named Sylvie who was 5 years old and one about 2 years old called Agnes. Jean believed in eating good and his wife was a very good cook. I had some french food that I had never heard about and that sent me. Little Sylvie, I adopted as my little mamma, because she was with me all the time I was awake and would get me a glass of cognac or whatever I wanted to drink wheever I asked her. I let her blow my horn and she really got a sound out…

I was so happy about being in France that I celebrated every day with a fresh bottle of cognac which I kept in my room and was drinking 15 to 20 glasses of cognac in bars and sidewalke cafes. But after a few weeks, my lips began to get dry and I could not play the way I was supposed to. I knew that it was from drinking too much, and although I was never drunk, I knew I had to stop drinking until my lips became right, and I did stop for at least one month.
